moat_against: Fee compression — custody and servicing are basis-point-priced scale games; BNY and State Street are larger
Market-linked revenue — servicing fees and AUM ride equity/bond market levels; a drawdown cuts fees mechanically
Rate sensitivity — net interest income ($2,411.0M in FY2025) depends on the yield curve and deposit repricing, outside management control
Capital-constrained bank model — growth and buybacks compete for regulatory capital; credit cycle exposure on the loan book
Expense pressure — noninterest expense rose in H1 2026, including Q2 2026 charges for software dispositions, severance and a one-time equity grant
moat_for: Custody scale oligopoly — $20.0T assets under custody/administration at Q2 2026; one of three global custody majors
High switching costs — custody, fund administration and asset servicing are operationally embedded in institutional clients
Recurring trust-fee base — trust, investment and other servicing fees $5,017.8M in FY2025, +6% YoY; eight straight quarters of positive organic fee growth to Q2 2026
Wealth franchise — $534B wealth-management AUM at Q2 2026 in UHNW / family-office niches with sticky relationships
Through-cycle profitability — return on average common equity 14.4% in FY2025; net income positive and substantial every year in the filed history
moat_justification: Moderate custody-bank moat: asset servicing is a scale oligopoly (BNY, State Street, Northern Trust) with deep operational integration and high switching costs for institutional clients — $20.0 trillion assets under custody/administration and $2.0 trillion AUM at June 30, 2026, trust fees growing organically for eight consecutive quarters, and return on average common equity of 14.4% in FY2025. Capped at 6 because custody fees are basis-point-priced and compressing, the larger rivals out-scale it, fee revenue rides market levels, net interest income is rate-driven, and as a bank its earnings are capital-constrained and cycle-exposed. A 6 gives CAP 9.8 years.
name: Northern Trust Corporation
one_liner: Quality custody bank, moat 6/10 — normalized OE base is credible but the OCF-based model fits a bank poorly; weighted IRR 12.53% (IV@15% $127.06 vs $161.34) is Tier C at low confidence, and it clears 15% only at or below ~$127.
sector: Finance / Asset servicing & wealth management (custody bank)
